issues.failure_explanation: The bound on \|f\|_{W^{n,r}(\Omega)} features the factor |\Omega|^{-d/p} \|\chi_\Omega\|_{\mathscr{F}L^s}. For an expanding family of balls \Omega = B_R(0), \|\chi_{B_R}\|_{\mathscr{F}L^s} scales as R^{d(1 - 1/s)}, whereas |\Omega|^{-d/p} scales as R^{-d^2/p} (or R^{-d/p}). For a fixed non-zero function f in the space, as R \to \infty, the left-hand side \|f\|_{W^{n,r}(B_R)} increases to \|f\|_{W^{n,r}(\mathbf{R}^d)} > 0, while the right-hand side tends to 0 whenever 1 - 1/s < d/p, yielding a contradiction. The proof incorrectly introduces a window g depending on the domain radius R into the modulation norm while treating the equivalence constants as independent of R.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must correctly track the dependence of the modulation-STFT window constants on the domain diameter rather than introducing a negative power of the domain volume.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 8 and its immediate consequences (Corollary 9 and Proposition 10) are mathematically false as stated.
issues.title: Sobolev-modulation embedding bound vanishes as the domain expands
issues.why_classification: The stated inequality is false for expanding domains and cannot be repaired without rethinking the embedding estimate and retracting the claimed negative power of |\Omega|.

issues.failure_explanation: For a convex set \Omega \subset \mathbf{R}^d, the Minkowski sum \Omega + \Omega equals the scaled set 2\Omega. Under Lebesgue measure in \mathbf{R}^d, |2\Omega| = 2^d |\Omega|, which means |\Omega + \Omega|^{1/p} = 2^{d/p} |\Omega|^{1/p}. The proof confuses vector scaling with volume scaling, omitting the dimension exponent d. Consequently, the constant 2 in Corollary 13, Proposition 17, and Corollary 18 should be 2^d (or 2^{d/p}).

failure_location.quote:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2^{1/p} by 2^{d/p} in Corollary 13, and replace the coefficient 2 by 2^d in the convex cases of Proposition 17 and Corollary 18.
issues.overall_effect: The convex-domain bounds in Corollary 13, Proposition 17, and Corollary 18 are understated by a factor of 2^{d(1/p - 1)} or 2^{d-1}.
issues.title: Incorrect volume scaling of Minkowski sum for convex domains
issues.why_classification: A routine correction of multivariable volume scaling repairs the statement and proofs of all affected results without altering the proof architecture or approximation rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: At this step, in order to obtain a uniform upper bound, it is necessary to assume that the set $\Omega\subset \rrd$ is bounded.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 19 fixes a bounded domain \Omega \subset \mathbf{R}^d and restricts the spatial shifts y of dictionary \mathbb{D}_\Omega to \Omega. However, every atom in \mathbb{D}_\Omega is spatially localized in \Omega and decays rapidly outside \Omega. Any linear combination f_N \in \Sigma_N(\mathbb{D}_\Omega) must therefore be concentrated near \Omega. If f \in M^{p,q}_m(\mathbf{R}^d) has support far away from \Omega, \|f - f_N\|_{W^{n,r}(\mathbf{R}^d)} cannot be made arbitrarily small, let alone bounded by C N^{-1/2} \|f\|_{M^{p,q}_m}. In the proof, the STFT inversion formula integrates over y \in \mathbf{R}^d, but the author claims this defines a representing measure supported on \tilde{\mathbb{D}}_\Omega (where y \in \Omega). If y were allowed to vary over \mathbf{R}^d, the dictionary atoms would fail to be uniformly bounded in W^{n,r}(\mathbf{R}^d), defeating Maurey's theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must require an unbounded dictionary or restrict the target function class and domain appropriately, which requires an entirely different proof framework to obtain uniform dictionary bounds.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 19 and its Corollaries 21 and 22 (global approximation on \mathbf{R}^d for weighted Feichtinger algebra and potential Sobolev spaces) are completely invalidated.
issues.title: Global Sobolev approximation on R^d using dictionary spatially restricted to a bounded set
issues.why_classification: The claim that a dictionary localized to a fixed bounded domain can approximate arbitrary functions on all of \mathbf{R}^d is fundamentally false, invalidating Theorem 19 and all its downstream corollaries.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\bigl|V_\varphi \sigma(x,\omega)\bigr|
\;\geq\; |T_2(x,\omega)| - |T_1(x,\omega)|
= \frac{1}{2\pi}\,e^{-\pi x^2} - |T_1(x,\omega)|.
\]
This implies the lower bound \eqref{eq:lowerbound}.

If it vanished at any real point $(x_0,\omega_0)$, then by the identity theorem for analytic functions it would vanish on a non-empty open set, and hence on the entire real plane (since the real plane has accumulation points).

issues.failure_explanation: The strict lower bound |V_\varphi \sigma(x,\omega)| > \frac{1}{2\pi} e^{-\pi x^2} is false: for \omega = 0 and x < 0, V_\varphi \sigma(x, 0) = \int_0^\infty t e^{-\pi(t-x)^2} dt < \frac{1}{2\pi} e^{-\pi x^2}, and for large negative x it decays exponentially faster than e^{-\pi x^2}. In the proof, the deduction of |A+B| > |A| from |A+B| \ge |A| - |B| is an elementary algebra fallacy. Furthermore, the non-vanishing claim is justified by asserting that if an analytic function vanishes at a point, the identity theorem implies it vanishes on an open set, which is mathematically false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must retract both the false uniform lower bound and the faulty identity-theorem argument, reducing the claim to the existence of points (t,\tau) where V_\varphi \sigma(t,\tau) \ne 0.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary 30 is false and unsupported as stated. (Condition (A) in the main paper only requires non-vanishing at a single point (t,\tau) with \tau \ne 0, which holds by continuity near (0,0), so the defect is isolated to Corollary 30).
issues.title: False strict lower bound and non-vanishing claim for STFT of ReLU
issues.why_classification: The primary claims of Corollary 30 (global non-vanishing and uniform lower bound) are false and unsupported, with no surviving comparable version of the primary result.
